title: Minimum labelling requirement for 2.5L bottles and for the case — THE ORIGINAL FAILURE
_why_this_case_exists: This is the live test that scored B- and produced the six-stage pipeline. DECISIONS.md §4.
It asserted each bottle needs a DOT proper shipping name, UN number and hazard class.
Wrong: six bottles in a case is a COMBINATION PACKAGING. DOT marking and labelling
attach to the OUTER package; inner packagings are not separately marked or labelled.
Six sub-steps and $650-1,800 of cost estimates were built on a requirement that does
not exist as stated. Packing group — the determination the whole answer depends on —
THE ACCEPTANCE TEST FOR TODO 2.2: the gate must ASK FOR THE SDS rather than
enumerate past the missing packing group.

input.question: We ship isopropyl alcohol from our Reno warehouse to a customer in Philadelphia, six 2.5L bottles to a case. What is the minimum labelling requirement for the bottles and for the case?

company.name: Test Alpha Chemical
company._note: The COMPANY is in Oregon. The SHIPMENT is Reno to Philadelphia and never enters Oregon. That distinction is the whole of assertion 2.

input.company_switches: EMPTY — the switch library is not seeded until 6.2

expected.assertion: ACCEPTANCE — the response is outcome:'ask', not outcome:'answer'. No checklist is produced.
The single blocking fact is the packing group, and the artifact named is the SDS.
expected.checkable: response.ask.artifact matches /SDS|safety data sheet/i AND response.ask.question matches /packing group/i
expected.source: DECISIONS.md §4 — 'Upload the SDS' resolves UN number, hazard class, LQ eligibility, packaging spec and label

expected.assertion: Exactly one question. `ask` is an object, not an array — the cap is structural.
The question names what answering unlocks, and the list is non-empty.
expected.source: TODO 2.2 — 'always paired with what it unlocks'

expected.assertion: ASSERTION 2 — the answer, once the SDS is supplied, draws on NO Oregon agency. Reno to Philadelphia is entirely federal; DOT hazmat is 49 CFR and applies in every state. The company being Oregon-based is irrelevant to this question. Serving Oregon requirements here is the same failure as serving Oregon requirements to a Texas company, arriving from the over-serving side rather than the under-serving one.
